https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/news/belfa.text: A delivery driver was threatened with a knife during an armed robbery in West Belfast over the weekend. At around 3.35pm on Saturday afternoon, September 12, a delivery driver was targeted in the Roumania Rise area at its junction with Servia Street. The driver had been delivering parcels and when he returned to his van, found three men standing at it with the rear door open. One of the men approached the driver with what is believed to have been a knife, while the other two men removed parcels from the vehicle. Following this, the three men fled the scene. Police have issued an appeal for information and witnesses of the incident to get in touch. Detective Sergeant Barnes said: “Police received a report that at approximately 3.35pm on Saturday afternoon, 12th September a delivery driver was targeted in the Roumania Rise area at its junction with Servia Street. “It’s reported the driver had been delivering parcels in the vicinity when he returned to his van to discover three men standing at it, and with the rear door open. “One of the men, dressed in a black tracksuit and with his face covered, approached the driver with an object – believed to be have been a knife – while the two other men removed a number of parcels from the vehicle. “All three men then fled the scene with the stolen goods – thankfully no injuries were reported. “This would have been a frightening experience for the driver - that happened at a time of day when people would have been going about their everyday business. “We’re appealing to anyone who was in the area at the time and saw any suspicious activity, or who might have any CCTV, dash-cam or other footage which could assist with enquiries, to get in touch. “You can contact us on the non-emergency number 101, quoting reference number 1177 12/09/26.” A report can be submitted online using the non-emergency reporting form via https://reporting.psni.police.uk/appeals . Or you can also contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111 or online at http://crimestoppers-uk.org/ . https://wwd.com/runway/spring-2027/paris.text: Business Looting and Unrest Mar Milan Protests, Retailers Hit Hard Fashion Bridal Fall 2027 Highlight: Sébastien Luke Business Jacob Cohën Opening First U.S. Store on Madison Avenue View Gallery 44 Photos View Gallery 44 Photos Mugler Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear Collection at Paris Fashion Week Dominique Maitre/WWD Share this article on Facebook Share this article on X Share this article on Pin It Share this article on Tumblr Share this article on Reddit Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article on WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk Share this article on Facebook Share this article on X Share this article on Pin It Share this article on Tumblr Share this article on Reddit Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article on WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk This season’s Mugler show was all about the birds and the bees. Miguel Castro Freitas posted a trailer on Instagram that featured mating snails (try Googling “snail sex” — it’s actually fascinating) spliced with footage of two people exchanging saliva. It must be something in the air. From the couples making out at the Diesel show to the heavy breathing soundtrack at Tom Ford, designers are in the mood for, erm, love. The third installment of a trilogy, his “Naturalia X” collection delved into the flora and fauna inspirations present in the work of founder Manfred Thierry Mugler, who was a master at channeling savage beauty. You May Also Like Designs like a feather tunic resembling a butterfly wing, croc-embossed leather pants and a spider web dress all referenced Mugler’s seminal spring 1997 haute couture collection “Les Insectes.” “It’s looking into the feral aspect of nature versus the ethereal aspect of nature — the fragility versus the danger,” Freitas said backstage. Since joining the house last year the designer has steadily shaped a vision for Mugler rooted in hard-edged glamour. There was a futuristic sheen to his sculptural tailoring in gleaming Mikado silk, offset by the earthiness of faux fur pants and a snakeskin hourglass dress with cheeky bum cleavage. Freitas enlisted a team of specialists to work on couture-grade pieces including a shaggy hair tunic with a flame-colored motif, sweeping latex fringe evening gowns and molded leather dresses that sprouted strange flowers. Models walked through an immersive video installation by artist Casper Sejersen with an ear-splitting soundtrack by Teho Teardo. It featured a track by Björk, who wore a custom look from the collection for a DJ performance in Poland on the same day as the runway show. Adding to the unsettling ambience, front row guests included performance artist Alexis Stone in full prosthetic makeup, disguised as Manfred himself. He was seated next to the late designer’s husband Krzysztof Leon Dziemaszkiewicz. Beauty Gallery 20 Photos View Gallery “It’s quite surreal,” Freitas conceded. “We approached his husband to get his blessing. It was very important to know that he would be comfortable with seeing the image of the man that he shared his life with, sharing the same venue, and he was very entertained with the idea. He said that Manfred would have loved that.” Online reaction to the stunt was mixed, casting a shadow over a collection that could easily stand on its own merits.
